music-audio.title: Music and audio
music-audio.status: Setup and assertions reviewed in the named score, cue, audio-engine and music-tool files. Telephone authority remains with #1609. No listening or browser run is claimed.
music-audio.keepSummary: audio resource limits and deterministic scheduling, the approved score structure, and explicit event-to-sound routing
protections: Audio scheduling avoids duplicate notes, non-finite start times and stale timelines after sailing.
Voice caps, output meters and overload recovery keep sound within its resource limits.
The score keeps the 32-bar ABAC form, alto range, wave transitions and chosen-night structure.
Injected events produce one cue at the right beat, distance and game-clock phase.
Potion sound routes fade back to dry audio and release their sources.

groups.title: Audio safety, scheduling and sample integrity
groups.question: Keep audio integrity checks unchanged?
groups.reason: Clocks and audio nodes are controlled stand-ins. Note uniqueness, finite scheduling, gate reset, bounded voices, drift recovery and compiled-voice determinism are pipeline guarantees, not outcomes of a generated fight. The sample manifest test enforces the existing licence/size contract. The old FOF implementation remains a lab comparison; its safety test does not select it as the game's voice.
examples: never schedules a sixteenth twice when the game runs slower than the audio or hitches (round 13: the music crackling, then quiet)
lets a greater sound cut the least short
a bar rendered across a reset (a new night: the timeline not anchored) is dropped, not started at a non-finite time
exampleLabels: Hitches never schedule a note twice.
A louder effect can replace a quieter voice at the cap.
A stale rendered bar never starts at NaN.

groups.title: Score form and explicit musical rules
groups.question: Keep current score contracts unchanged?
groups.reason: The planner receives synthetic wave clocks; the score receives explicit seeds and styles. Assertions directly implement the 9 Oct ABAC structure, 11 Oct nightly set and 14 Oct alto/stepwise redesign. A 30-minute planner loop is not a played night. The 120 BPM test supplies its own style-based beat tuning; it does not prohibit choosing a different record. Wide instrument phrases, retained soprano fallback and alternate lab arpeggios are explicit comparison modes, not stale default singer claims.
examples: is ABAC in 8-bar phrases, A coming back exactly, B and C different
sings as an alto, G3 to G4 in the home key, whatever the seed
changes at least two of genre, key, lead, bass, voice and density every wave (never the tempo: the gameplay's), and never the genre twice running
exampleLabels: A 32-bar tune returns to its first phrase.
The singer stays within the approved alto range.
Each wave changes at least two musical features.

groups.title: Cue boundaries, potion routing and music-tool data
groups.question: Keep cue and audio data rules unchanged?
groups.reason: Tests inject the watch, cleared-area, fireworks or knockdown event, manually advance clocks and log a fake sound call. Counts here prove exactly-once routing and configured limits. The inland sea-life case is the negative range boundary. Potion tests directly set trip times and check routing, fade and source disposal. Music Lab JSON/MIDI tests use synthetic input and roundtrip/validation assertions. The first sound.test authority case is excluded for #1609.
examples: plays once, on the next half-beat after the areaCleared event, louder near the new soundsystem
routes both dry and filtered paths, starts dry and restores dry gain after Stop
copies only what changed, and pastes back the same
exampleLabels: A clearing event sounds once on the next half-beat.
Stopping a potion restores dry sound.
Copied Music Lab settings round-trip exactly.

groups.title: Generated cue rates and melody proportions
groups.question: Make these three rate/proportion tests informational? Yes moves the 60/600-second dolphin/kraken counts and 60-seed melody-pace survey to a nightly report; range, routing, note validity and explicit form rules keep blocking releases.
groups.reason: Sea-life tests sample seeded timetables for 60/600 seconds and require at least three splashes or one groan. Melody pace samples 60 seeds × ABC, requiring <3.5 notes/bar, >1 whole note/phrase and >15% triplets. These quantify an intended feel; they do not establish no-NaN, ownership or exactly-once event delivery. Opposite-coast absence assertions in the mixed sea-life cases must first be retained as small range tests.
examples: by the east coast, the dolphins' splashes, now and then
by the west coast, the kraken's groan and the water pouring off it, rarely
is mostly slow, with whole notes and triplets often, and some busier bars
exampleLabels: Dolphins splash at least three times in a minute.
The kraken groans during a ten-minute sample.
Generated phrases exceed a triplet-share target.

groups.title: Outdated cheer-test descriptions
groups.question: Update these two test descriptions to the current knockdown design? Yes removes the old +1 BPM and rewind wording; the existing one-cheer/on-return timing assertions stay unchanged.
groups.reason: The suite still says +1 BPM (7 Oct), and a case name says after trumpet and rewind. The 9 Oct design instead adds 5 BPM and removes the rewind at the cut. Neither case asserts +1 or requires a rewind: one calls knockdownTempo with current tuning; the other supplies a synthetic return clock. This is stale explanation, not obsolete behavior or deletion authority.
examples: with no knockout under way, cheers once, on the bar line the tempo starts rising from
knocked down, cheers once as she's back at her decks (after the trumpet and the rewind), on her clock
exampleLabels: A tempo change cheers once on the next bar.
Returning to the decks cheers once on her clock.

rulings: M5 old: tempoUp.cues.test.ts suite cites Ed, 2026-10-07, ‘+1 BPM’, and the second test names ‘the trumpet and the rewind’. Replacement: Ed, 2026-10-09, docs/notes/music.md Beat clock: ‘it stays at 120 unless you are knocked down, in which case it gains 5bpm’; Form: ‘the rewind at the cut is gone’. The assertions already test current event timing; only their description is proposed for rewrite.

M2 old singer: docs/notes/music.md records the 11 Oct choice ‘e Recorded + ethereal will do for now’. Replacement: 14 Oct singer redesign specifies alto, narrow stepwise phrases and two effect chains. musicForm.test.ts asserts MIDI55–67, limited leaps, voice only in builds/breakdowns, and pure-chain chorus/octave/shimmer zero. No old high-soprano default is pinned by this reviewed group; the old soprano is explicitly fallback/comparison data.

M4 current intent: Ed, 2026-10-09, musicForm.test.ts: ‘keep the melodies relatively slow, but not always. Use whole notes and triplets quite often’. The numeric 3.5/15% thresholds are implementation interpretations of that intent, not quoted numeric rulings. Sea-life header cites Ed, 2026-10-07, dolphins east/kraken west, but the ≥3/≥1 sampled counts are not quoted frequency decisions. No newer cancellation of these effects is claimed.

M2 tempo scope: records were extended on 29 Oct to 100–200 BPM, with 100/120 starters (recordSave.test.ts). musicForm's 120-BPM case builds t.beat from style.bpm explicitly; it checks wave changes do not choose tempo. docs/notes/music.md 11 Oct: ‘tempo is set by the gameplay’. This does not contradict selectable records.
